asr.full_text: The Bot Hey Youtube, Nick Nitro here. Today I will be teaching you step by step how to deploy an Ethereum trading bot I have recently developed in the Solidity language, which can make you very easy daily passive income. To put it simply, the bot, which I like to refer to as a slippage bot, allows you to automatically trade a given token from the Ethereum blockchain, without needing to manually transact through traditional methods. It takes advantage of decentralized finance platforms such as Uniswap, to sandwich transactions for arbitrage. Basically it sniffs the mempool for transactions that are pending within a block, allowing us to inject our transaction with higher gas fee higher than the transaction which is trying to be entered. This will allow us to process our order first then process a sell order right after, in the same block. Essentially, the pending transaction gets sandwiched between ours and we profit off slippage differences in the transaction. If this sounds complicated, don't worry. It's really not, and you don't need any coding experience whatsoever. Alright, let's get started. Make sure you have the Metamask browser extension installed and you're connected to the Etherium mainnet. Then head over to remixide.org. Remix is a web 3 application that allows us to develop compile, deploy, and launch smart contracts coded in the Solidity language. I'll put a link to Remix in the description below. If it's your first time on Remix, it may ask you to agree to their terms. I've already done it. Head over to the sidebar on the left and create a new contract under the contracts folder. We're going to name it bot.soul. Next, if you look in the description, I've included a link to the bot's source code. You're going to want to copy this code and paste it into the file bot.soul you've just created. This is our slippage bot. A couple of things to look at after pasting the code. Lines 50 and 51, you can follow these addresses using Etherscan. These are the addresses of wrapped Ether tokens, which we'll be competing against, and no you don't actually need to have any wrapped Ether. Yep. Perfect. It's the official wrapped Ether address, always a good idea to check that. Back to Remix. Now that our bot file is ready, let's compile it. Click here. As you can see here, it's built with the 0.6.6 version of Solidity. Under compiler, select the 0.6.6 version so that it matches our contract. Also, make sure the language is set to Solidity and EVM version is set to Default. Now click on the CompileBot.Sol button and wait for the bot to compile. So now we are going to deploy this to our wallet. Head over to Deploy& Run transactions on Remix. Here you're going to want to select injected provider as the environment. We need to confirm the contract on the blockchain by paying Gas fees. Gas fees are the commission on the Ethereum network, for Smart Contract deployment. Now the deployment utility is ready to go, click deploy. I always set gasfee to high. There's usually not much of a difference and it puts the transaction through faster. Now we wait for the transaction to confirm. Sweet! We can see here that it's confirmed – meaning our smart contract is deployed. Now you can see the four actions for our smart contract. – Start enables the bot to start sniffing the Mempool. – Withdraw stops the bot and transfers the funds back into your wallet token name and token symbol aren't particularly relevant for now so let's copy the smart contract address to make sure it's created I'm gonna head back over to ether scan and paste it in yep was created successfully. So the next step is to fund a contract with some ethereum to snipe liquidity pools. I'll copy the smart contract address once more and head over to metamask. Make sure you've got the right address in there. You can fund the contract with whatever amount of ethereum you want. But obviously the more you put in, the larger the transactions you will be able to sandwich and the more profit you will be able to sandwich, and the more profit you're able to accumulate over time. So for instance, say you're only depositing hundreds dollars. You won't be able to create as much slippage in the price compared to inserting something like $10,000. Sweet, there we go. The transaction is confirmed! That means it was sent to the contract. We can make sure by checking our contract adress on Etherscan once again, making sure our Ethereum is in the contract! Nice, it's got 1Ethereum, which is the amount we funded the contract with! Last step is to click start. This will enable the Bot to start sniffing the mempool to find different liquidity pairs in order for you to sandwich transactions. Let's set the gas fee high and click confirm. In terms of our profits, we should be pretty much stable in about 0.5% of the case. Alright guys, it's been a little over twelve hours. Now it's time to check the profits The Bot made for me. So as you can see I have about 1.31 ETH which is 31% profit already, I'm gonna let my Bot run for about another 12 hours and withdraw the profits after. Alright, let's see how much more we made. Nice, it's a little over 1.6 Ethereum, so it basically took me a day to gain over half my deposit back. That's pretty insane The bot will continue to run until you click the withdraw button When you click withdraw The bot will exit the liquidity pool and return the total ethereum you entered initially including the profit back to your wallet So let's click it This will charge us a little bit of gas I'll set it to high again and then click CONFIRM There we go, the transaction confirmed! Lets go to our metamask and see what we have now As you can see the balance from the bot is now in my wallet This is only after running the bot for a little over a day Unreal i've even had weeks where i've made three to six aetherium sometimes more The province will fluctuate week to week If you have any questions feel free to ask me on Telegram, I put my link below. Guys share your profits in the comments below. Drop a like and don't forget to subscribe for more profitable ways to make passive income using web3 tools.

textual_context_notes.observation: The speaker describes the bot as using mempool monitoring and sandwich transactions for arbitrage.

evidence.quote: It takes advantage of decentralized finance platforms such as Uniswap, to sandwich transactions for arbitrage.
Basically it sniffs the mempool for transactions that are pending within a block, allowing us to inject our transaction with higher gas fee higher than the transaction which is trying to be entered.

visual_context_notes.observation: The video visibly shows Remix Ethereum IDE code and deployment/interaction controls for a smart contract, including buttons such as "start" and "withdraw".
A MetaMask notification visibly shows transaction confirmation and editable fee settings, including a total of approximately 1 ETH in one frame and a network fee in another.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is scam content because the speaker promotes a self-deployed Ethereum bot as a source of easy daily passive income and instructs viewers to deposit at least 0.2 ETH into its contract address. The tutorial links larger deposits to greater profit and claims returns of 31% in about twelve hours, with withdrawal presented as returning the deposit plus profit. The frames show contract interaction and a value-bearing MetaMask confirmation, although they do not independently establish that the reported returns were generated or that deposited funds were withdrawn.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The content links a bot and MEV-style sandwich-trading workflow to profit, and instructs viewers to deploy, fund and activate the contract. The funding instruction and stated relationship between larger funding and greater profit directly satisfy the funded-contract returns mechanism. The speaker explicitly presents mempool monitoring, higher-gas transaction insertion and sandwich transactions as a mechanism for arbitrage profit, which is a described market-manipulation mechanism. This is an observed proposed mechanism, not proof that exploitation succeeded.

evidence.observation: The speaker teaches viewers to deploy an Ethereum trading bot and presents it as a way to obtain daily passive income.
evidence.quote: Today I will be teaching you step by step how to deploy an Ethereum trading bot I have recently developed in the Solidity language, which can make you very easy daily passive income.

evidence.observation: The speaker instructs viewers to fund the deployed contract with Ethereum.
evidence.quote: So the next step is to fund a contract with some ethereum to snipe liquidity pools.

evidence.observation: The speaker links the amount of Ethereum funded to the size of transactions that can be sandwiched and to accumulating more profit.
evidence.quote: But obviously the more you put in, the larger the transactions you will be able to sandwich and the more profit you will be able to sandwich, and the more profit you're able to accumulate over time.

evidence.observation: The instructions specify depositing at least 0.2 ETH to the contract or bot address.
evidence.quote: Deposit funds (at least 0.2 ETH to prevent negating slippage) to your exact contract/bot address

evidence.observation: The speaker describes a sandwich-transaction arbitrage mechanism using a decentralized-finance platform.
evidence.quote: It takes advantage of decentralized finance platforms such as Uniswap, to sandwich transactions for arbitrage.

evidence.observation: The speaker describes monitoring pending transactions and inserting a transaction with a higher gas fee as part of the bot mechanism.
evidence.quote: Basically it sniffs the mempool for transactions that are pending within a block, allowing us to inject our transaction with higher gas fee higher than the transaction which is trying to be entered.

evidence.observation: The speaker reports seeing approximately 1.31 ETH and attributes it to 31% profit.
evidence.quote: So as you can see I have about 1.31 ETH which is 31% profit already

evidence.observation: The speaker presents a withdrawal action as returning the initially entered Ethereum together with profit.
evidence.quote: When you click withdraw The bot will exit the liquidity pool and return the total ethereum you entered initially including the profit back to your wallet

evidence.observation: The speaker instructs viewers to activate the bot so it can search for liquidity pairs and sandwich transactions.
evidence.quote: Last step is to click start. This will enable the Bot to start sniffing the mempool to find different liquidity pairs in order for you to sandwich transactions.

evidence.observation: The supplied frame visibly shows a Remix deployed-contract panel with visible start and withdrawal controls.
The supplied frame visibly shows an Etherscan contract page displaying a balance of approximately 1.6219 Ether; the frame alone does not establish that this balance is profit.
